meanings: Ebba (a cradle-name; no sense): old Ebba of Fenholm, Marl's grandmother
derivation: *ebb-ā > Hal ebbā > ebba: the feminine -a kept, as Bena, Denna (benā, dennā); a name: names are names (no sense given); unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: old Ebba (of Fenholm): the Book's 'old Ebba'
derivation: a phrase: Ebba (S05-01) + hemm 'old' (an adjective after the name; adjectives do not mutate, orrowen_v2 §3.3); not Hemma, which is the rank 'Elderess'; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: (new sense) a leaf of a tree, of a bough; pl. flenneth, leaves (beside the irregular flennath, the Book)
derivation: the existing O0614 flenn 'a leaf of a book or of slate' (Hal hwlennā) read of a tree: the same new sense as W03-01 (wf12), reached here independently, to be merged into O0614 (one form, one row). The tree's leaves (flenneth) and the Book's (flennath) part only by the harmony of the ending; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: a swallow ('mortar-bird': the bird that builds its nest of mud under an arch); pl. lodhnasath
derivation: compound: lodh 'mortar' (*loð-) + nas 'a bird' (*nas-; n unchanged as the second element, §3.10): a masons' name for the bird that lays mortar, in the lexicon's own field (to build is to lay; the small words are the mortar); unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: a hawk ('chase-bird'); pl. ganurnasath
derivation: compound: ganur 'chase, drive before one' (*ganur-) + nas 'a bird' (*nas-; n unchanged), as ganurard 'a hunter'; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: a whistle; (v.) whistle ('breath-song'); hossvell X dem susk, whistle X up (a wind)
derivation: compound: hoss 'breath' (*hoss-) + vell 'a song; sing' (*fell-; v unchanged as the second element): the form S03-04, S08 and S09 (wf12) reached, taken here so that one whistle serves the Book (S07's inthvell and S02's hoss vell are the same thought). Lanner's breath-song calls up the sky-breath, helvhoss; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: an anvil ('hammer-stone'); pl. drunndholmath
derivation: compound: drunn 'a mallet, a hammer' (*drunn-) + S·tolm 'a stone' (t > dh, as gorndholm, trenndholm); unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: a far-glass, a spyglass ('a glass to far off'); pl. sirreth dem neld; ul ol sirreth dem neld, 'into our far-glasses'
derivation: a phrase: sirr 'glass' (*sirr-) + dem neld 'away, far off' (O0393): W12-S02-12's form, taken so that Pellow's glass has one name in the Book; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: a knuckle ('finger-quoin'); pl. nindyornath
derivation: compound: nind 'a finger' (*niʔnd-) + S·gorn 'a corner, a quoin' (g > y before a vowel), as gemmyorn 'a square' and haldyorn 'a wall-corner'; the masons' word for the corner of the hand. Said so because derd nind 'finger-bone' softens to rerd ('the sun') after lo, hy, um; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: a cough ('a broken breath')
derivation: a phrase: hoss 'breath' (*hoss-) + gask 'broken' (*gaʔsk-; an adjective after its noun); unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: (new sense) a nest: a bird's place (beside 'a rookery')
derivation: nas 'a bird' + -ow (place): the existing O1665 nasow, 'a rookery, a place of birds', read of one bird's place; to be merged into O1665 as a further sense (one form, one row); unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: (new sense) a course-stone: a stone of a house's course, kept when the house is lost (Ebba's, out of Fenholm), heard as 'the tale-stone'
derivation: canon trenn + S·tolm: the existing O2582 trenndholm 'the tale-stone ('the course-stone')' in its plain sense; to be merged into O2582 (one form, one row). The stone passed at the hearth and the stone of a house's last course are one word; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: (new sense) clear (a place) of a thing: lunn X hy Y, 'make room in X from Y'; sweep clear
derivation: canon lunn 'open, make room' with hy 'from': to be merged into O1278 (one form, one row); unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: (new sense) (et Orrol) the Road: the column's march up the mountain after the Fall
derivation: orr 'go' + -Ol, the existing O1878 orrol 'a road ('a going')', as a name; to be merged into O1878; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: ere, before (of a clause): somm nath … tul, 'while … not yet'
derivation: a phrase: somm 'while' + nath NEG(+N), with tul 'yet' after the verb (nath … tul is 'not yet', orrowen_v2 §3.8); not amm nath, which is 'unless' (O0015); unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: No, I will stand (the teller who refuses the seat: 'I do not sit; I will stand')
derivation: a phrase: nath NEG(+N) + reskym sit-1SG + es FUT(+N) + stonom stand-1SG; pilot I.1's answer to the offered seat, which v3 gives in I.1, III.1, III.2, V.5 and VI.1; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

orrowen: ketha so, hy vodh dossant lor
meanings: hold them, for they are ours ('keep them, for they are at us')
derivation: a phrase: ketha hold-IMP.PL + so them + hy vodh because + dossant be-3PL + lor at-1PL (the 'at' idiom of having); III.1 (Amm sy hunna vollath et cummath, eth ketha so, …), and the same words in V.5 and VI.1; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)
book_lemmas: hold them, for they are ours

meanings: The sea hath not finished ('the sea does not finish yet'): Corlen's saying; in a past telling eth nath re dhunn et wadh tul, 'and the sea had not finished' (III.2)
derivation: a phrase: nath NEG(+N) + dunn N·tunn 'finish, complete' + et wadh 'the sea' + tul 'yet' (nath … tul 'not yet', orrowen_v2 §3.8): the second half of S08-08 (wf12, V.5: Tovv. Nath dunn et wadh tul.), the same words; III.1 has Tovva, to many, because Corlen says it to the young men and his gunners; the Epilogue says it again; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: Look close ('look near'): Pellow's word, held up with his glass; 1sg past Re veskym virr, 'I looked close'
derivation: a phrase: veska see-IMP.PL + virr 'near; close'; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

orrowen: Doss maver vothol reller um hos
meanings: Someone must keep a light ('need of tending a lamp is upon someone'): Hesk's word
derivation: a phrase: doss maver um 'must' (O0488, the 'upon' idiom, with the verbal noun as S04's doss maver stonol um) + vothol tending (voth + -Ol) + reller S·greller 'a lamp' (the possessor of the verbal noun; g dropped before r, as baegyth reller) + um upon + hos 'someone'; III.2 and VI.1; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: I swear to that. It stands (Kael's oath on a fact, closed as every oath closes)
derivation: a phrase: Rytom um (O2169) + ull 'that' + Ston (O2386, the close of an oath); pilot I.1's Rytom um ull pawast. Ston., without pawast; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

orrowen: Doss hulter stinet dem o yaldat, eth nath morr o hyo
meanings: A staff is cut for its work, and leaveth not its work (the law of the staff, as III.2 quotes it)
derivation: a phrase: doss + hulter 'a staff' + stinet cut (stin + -At) + dem 'for' (+N; o unchanged) + o its (+S) + yaldat S·galdat 'a work' + eth + nath NEG(+N) + morr N·orr 'go' + o + hyo 'out of it' (orr hy 'leave'); the rolls' line beside it: eth hulter stinet dem et galdat, 'and a staff cut for the work'. For the I.4 translator to take or overrule; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)

meanings: a street ('a town-walk', the going of a walled town); pl. hinnarorrolath; hinnarorrol et drunnardath, 'the street of the smiths'
derivation: compound: hinnar 'a walled town' (*xinnar-) + S·orrol 'a going, a road' (a vowel unchanged as the second element, §3.10), as haldorrol 'the wall-walk' (O0861): said so because um orrol et X is heard as 'upon the going of X' (blind back-translation of S05-III2-23: 'As the smiths left'), and ul orrol beds to ul morrol, 'in going'; unit S05 (III.1, III.2, wf12)
